ent-1x09: Disguised as locals on a pre-warp world, Archer's team traces a mysterious illness to Malurians secretly poisoning the water, and Archer teams up with a local woman, Riaan.
ent-1x10: Sent to aid the freighter Fortunate after a Nausicaan raid, Archer finds its resentful acting captain secretly holding a pirate prisoner and bent on revenge.
ent-1x11: Crewman Daniels reveals to Archer that he is an agent from the future, hunting the Suliban Silik, who has slipped aboard among a group of alien pilgrims.
ent-1x12: Silent aliens of unknown purpose attack Enterprise, forcing Reed and Trip to rush unfinished phase cannons online, while Hoshi hunts for Reed's favorite food for his birthday.
ent-1x13: Phlox finds a cure for the genetic plague killing the Valakians, but he and Archer withhold it so the planet's other species, the Menk, can evolve unhindered.
ent-1x14: Reed, Hoshi, and T'Pol board a crippled Klingon ship sinking into a gas giant and try to rescue its hostile crew as their own shuttlepod is stolen.
ent-1x15: The Vulcans blame Archer for P'Jem's destruction and recall T'Pol, but on Coridan the two are taken by rebels, and after Shran helps free them, the Vulcans relent.
ent-1x16: Mistaking debris for Enterprise's wreckage, Trip and Reed drift in a shuttlepod with dwindling air, bickering and bonding as they prepare to die, though the ship is intact.
ent-1x17: Enterprise meets the V'tosh ka'tur, Vulcans who have embraced emotion, and T'Pol's cautious exploration ends when their member Tolaris forces a mind meld on her.
ent-1x18: On the sunless rogue planet Dakala, visions of a woman lead Archer to a shape-shifting species hunted for sport by the Eska, and he helps it escape them.
ent-1x19: Ferengi raiders knock out the crew and loot Enterprise, and Trip, spared because he was in decontamination, must stop them in little more than his underwear.
ent-1x20: The derelict ship Enterprise salvages is home to Ezral, a survivor who has recreated his dead crewmates as holograms, and his very real daughter, Liana.
ent-1x21: Straying into Tandaran space, Archer and Mayweather are held in an internment camp for Suliban civilians and, convinced of the detainees' innocence, help them break out.
ent-1x22: A web-spinning creature that slipped aboard during a tense Kreetassan visit snares Archer and others, and Hoshi works to communicate with it before the captives die.
ent-1x23: Archer ferries Vulcan Ambassador V'Lar, expelled from Mazar for alleged misconduct, as Mazarite ships give chase, and T'Pol's faith is rewarded when the charges prove a smear.
ent-1x24: Zobral, grateful for repairs, hosts Archer and Trip on his desert world but wants their help in his rebellion, leaving the pair stranded in searing heat under fire.
ent-1x25: Shore leave on Risa goes awry as Trip and Reed are robbed by shape-shifters, Archer's new companion hides an agenda, and an injured Travis needs a hibernating Phlox.
ent-1x26: After a shuttle launch seemingly wipes out a mining colony, Enterprise is recalled, until Daniels exposes Suliban sabotage and Archer is stranded with him in a ruined future.
ent-2x01: Stranded with Daniels in a devastated 31st century, Archer struggles to reach home while T'Pol's crew, held by the Suliban, fights to retake Enterprise and bring him back.
ent-2x02: Over dinner, T'Pol recounts how her great-grandmother T'Mir and two fellow Vulcans, stranded in 1957 Carbon Creek, Pennsylvania, passed as humans and came to care for the town.
ent-2x03: Enterprise hits a cloaked Romulan mine, and a second one latched to the hull pins Reed as he tries to defuse it, forcing Archer to cut him free.
ent-2x04: An automated repair station fixes Enterprise with suspicious ease, then fakes Mayweather's death to harvest his brain for its computer network, forcing the crew to rescue him.
ent-2x05: Archer frets through a night in sickbay beside Porthos, felled by an alien pathogen, while trying to mend relations with the Kreetassans, whom the dog has offended.
ent-2x06: Enterprise finds a mining colony extorted for its deuterium by Klingon raiders, and the crew trains the settlers to fight back, turning their fuel into a fiery trap.
ent-2x07: T'Pol asks Archer to help her capture Menos, a Vulcan agent gone rogue for two decades, a mission that unlocks memories she had suppressed of an earlier killing.
ent-2x08: Reed's forgotten communicator draws him and Archer back to a pre-warp world, where they are caught and condemned as spies until Trip arrives in a Suliban cell ship.
ent-2x09: Near a black hole, radiation drives the crew into obsessions, from Archer's writing to Trip's redesign of the captain's chair, leaving an unaffected T'Pol to save the ship.
ent-2x10: After her first transport, Hoshi seems to fade from the crew's sight and uncovers aliens planting a bomb, all in the seconds before her body rematerializes.
ent-2x11: Helping repair an alien ship, Trip wakes Kaitaama, a royal abducted for ransom and held in stasis, and ends up stranded with her on a remote planet.
ent-2x12: Sheltering from a lethal neutronic storm, the crew crams into a warp nacelle's catwalk for eight days, until Takret militia board the seemingly abandoned ship.
ent-2x13: Shot down by an Arkonian pilot, Trip is stranded with him on a moon whose sunrise brings lethal heat, and the rivals must overcome distrust to survive.
ent-2x14: Vulcans threaten T'Pol's post on Enterprise on learning she has Pa'nar Syndrome, a disease they link to shunned mind-melders, while Phlox's wife Feezal flirts with Trip.
ent-2x15: Shran asks Archer to mediate a standoff with the Vulcans over the disputed planetoid Weytahn, and Archer must get past a hotheaded Andorian lieutenant to broker a truce.
ent-2x16: Enterprise recovers a tiny time ship, larger inside than out, with a dead human pilot, and is caught between the Suliban and the Tholians, who both want it.
ent-2x17: Wrongly arrested by the Enolians, Archer and Trip are shipped toward the penal colony Canamar, and when a fellow prisoner hijacks the transport, Archer must outwit him.
ent-2x18: A huge vessel swallows Enterprise, and its noncorporeal occupants begin swapping places with crew members, including Trip, until T'Pol's disciplined mind and Phlox help drive them out.
ent-2x19: A Klingon tribunal tries Archer for aiding rebels, and despite the aging advocate Kolos's defense he is sentenced to Rura Penthe, from which Enterprise must spring him.
ent-2x20: After his father's death, Travis visits the family freighter Horizon, where he clashes with his brother Paul, now captain, before helping the crew fend off raiders.
ent-2x21: While Trip, Reed, and Mayweather descend caverns to evacuate Denobulan scientists from Xantoras, Phlox treats an Antaran patient who refuses care from a Denobulan.
ent-2x22: Trip secretly teaches a Vissian cogenitor, a third-gender being treated as property, to read, and when Archer denies it asylum, it takes its own life.
ent-2x23: Frozen Borg drones unearthed in the Arctic revive, assimilate their discoverers, and seize a ship, and Enterprise stops them only after they signal the Delta Quadrant.
ent-2x24: News of A.G. Robinson's death leads Archer to recount their rivalry as NX test pilots, including the unauthorized flight that broke the warp two barrier.
ent-2x25: Tellarite bounty hunter Skalaar abducts Archer to claim a Klingon reward, as a microbe sends T'Pol into pon farr while she is sealed in decon with Phlox.
ent-2x26: An alien probe kills seven million from Florida to Venezuela, and Enterprise, reinforced with MACO troops, heads into the Delphic Expanse to stop the Xindi from striking again.
ent-3x01: A freighter captain's tip sends Archer and Trip to a mining colony, where a Xindi laborer trades information for escape, a deal that goes badly wrong.
ent-3x02: Battered by spatial anomalies, Enterprise is looted by Osaarian pirates, and a hardened Archer threatens a captive in an airlock to track down the stolen supplies.
ent-3x03: A virus transforms Archer, Reed, and Hoshi into members of a long-extinct species, compelled to seek its lost city, as Phlox works on a cure.
ent-3x04: Archer rescues Rajiin from an alien slave market, but the refugee is a Xindi agent gathering biological data on humans, and Xindi soldiers board Enterprise to retrieve her.
ent-3x05: Inside an asteroid field, Enterprise finds the Vulcan ship Seleya crewed by maddened, zombielike Vulcans, and T'Pol begins succumbing to the same trellium-D poisoning.
ent-3x06: The telepath Tarquin offers to help find the Xindi weapon if Hoshi keeps him company in exile, and her stay reveals how deep his fixation runs.
ent-3x07: At a Xindi plant refining weapon-grade kemocite, Archer befriends Gralik, an Arboreal unaware of its purpose, and spares the facility in return for help tracking the shipment.
ent-3x08: Parasites rob Archer of new memories, and in a future where the Xindi have destroyed Earth, T'Pol, his caretaker, and Phlox seek a way to erase that timeline.
ent-3x09: Enterprise finds a frontier town of humans in the Expanse, descendants of people abducted from 19th-century Earth by the Skagarans, whom they overthrew and keep as an underclass.
ent-3x10: To save a comatose Trip, Phlox grows Sim, a fast-aging clone whose neural tissue can heal him, and the crew must reckon with Sim's wish to live.
ent-3x11: Sent back to 2004 Detroit by Daniels, Archer and T'Pol hunt three Xindi-Reptilians paying a small-time crook, Loomis, to deliver human blood for a bioweapon.
ent-3x12: Zealots who worship the Expanse's spheres as holy seize Enterprise with suicide bombers, intending to turn it against a rival sect, and Archer must outwit their leader, D'Jamat.
ent-3x13: Shran's warship turns up in the Expanse offering to help Enterprise find the Xindi test site, but his real orders are to steal the prototype weapon for Andoria.
ent-3x14: Having captured weapon designer Degra and erased his recent memories, Archer stages a ruse, posing as his cellmate years later, to learn where the Xindi weapon is built.
ent-3x15: Enterprise rescues an alien pilot from a spatial anomaly, Reed and MACO Major Hayes come to blows over their roles, and Trip and T'Pol's neuropressure sessions turn intimate.
ent-3x16: While the crew sleeps through a trans-dimensional disturbance, Phlox runs Enterprise alone with only T'Pol for company, until he realizes she is a figment of his strained mind.
ent-3x17: Sprayed by a chemical aboard a crashed Xindi-Insectoid ship, Archer becomes obsessed with saving its unhatched eggs, and the crew must mutiny to stop him.
ent-3x18: Captured on a one-way mission against the Xindi weapon at Azati Prime, Archer tries to convince Degra that humans are no enemy, while Xindi ships leave Enterprise crippled.
ent-3x19: With Enterprise crippled, Archer crosses a moral line and steals a warp coil from Illyrian travelers, while T'Pol confesses her trellium-D addiction to Phlox.
ent-3x20: Two Xindi councillors will halt the weapon if Archer proves the Xindi were deceived, as the crew mourns its dead and Trip writes to a fallen crewman's family.
ent-3x21: Enterprise meets an aged version of itself, crewed by descendants under Lorian, son of Trip and T'Pol, whose ship was flung back in time by a subspace corridor.
ent-3x22: Archer pleads his case before the Xindi Council with proof of the Sphere-Builders' deception, but the Reptilians and Insectoids seize the weapon, Degra is murdered, and Hayes dies.
ent-3x23: The Xindi-Reptilians abduct Hoshi to unlock the weapon's launch codes, and Archer joins friendly Xindi factions in a failed bid to stop the weapon from launching toward Earth.
ent-3x24: Archer destroys the Xindi weapon en route to Earth, seemingly at the cost of his life, while T'Pol cripples the sphere network; then Archer resurfaces in 1944.
ent-4x01: Enterprise arrives in a 1944 where the alien Na'kuhl have helped Nazi Germany invade America, and Archer, escaping capture, joins the Resistance in occupied New York.
ent-4x02: With Silik as an unlikely ally, Archer strikes at Vosk's time conduit, and its destruction restores history and ends the Temporal Cold War.
ent-4x03: Home at last, the crew scatters to face the Expanse's toll: Archer retreats with Captain Hernandez, Phlox meets human xenophobia, and T'Pol marries Koss on Vulcan.
ent-4x04: When genetically engineered Augments seize a Klingon ship, Archer enlists their imprisoned creator, Dr. Arik Soong, to find them, and Soong slips away to rejoin his children.
ent-4x05: Soong and his Augments seize Cold Station 12, a medical facility holding frozen Augment embryos and deadly pathogens, and threaten Phlox and its staff to get them.
ent-4x06: Malik plots to launch a bioweapon at a Klingon world to ignite war, and when Soong balks, his Augment children turn on him, leaving Archer to stop it.
ent-4x07: The bombing of Earth's embassy on Vulcan kills Admiral Forrest, and Archer and T'Pol cross the Forge to find the accused Syrrannites, as Archer receives Surak's katra.
ent-4x08: Among the Syrrannites, Archer wrestles with Surak's katra as it guides him to a lost relic, while V'Las orders their enclave bombed and readies a strike on Andoria.
ent-4x09: Archer and T'Pol bring the Kir'Shara, Surak's original teachings, before the Vulcan High Command to expose V'Las, while Enterprise wedges itself between Vulcan and Andorian fleets.
ent-4x10: Transporter inventor Emory Erickson's experiment aboard Enterprise is secretly a bid to retrieve his son Quinn, lost in subspace years earlier, and it ends in grief.
ent-4x11: Two Organians inhabit crew members to observe how Enterprise responds when Hoshi and Trip catch a lethal silicon-based virus, and Archer challenges the watchers to intervene.
ent-4x12: Ferrying Tellarite diplomats to talks with Andoria, Enterprise answers Shran's distress call, and the raider that destroyed his ship proves to be a disguised Romulan drone.
ent-4x13: Archer builds a joint fleet of humans, Andorians, Tellarites, and Vulcans to trap the Romulan drone, and must survive a ritual duel with Shran to hold it together.
ent-4x14: Discovering the Romulan drones are piloted telepathically, Archer and Shran seek out the Aenar, a blind Andorian subspecies, and the Aenar Jhamel helps reach her captive brother.
ent-4x15: Phlox is abducted by Klingons desperate to cure a plague born of their Augment experiments, as Trip transfers to Columbia and Section 31 presses Reed into service.
ent-4x16: Trip crosses from Columbia at warp to save a sabotaged Enterprise, and Phlox's cure halts the Klingon plague but leaves its victims without their forehead ridges.
ent-4x17: Three Orion women gifted to Archer use pheromones to seize control of the ship's men, and only Trip, shielded by his psychic bond with T'Pol, resists.
ent-4x18: A ruthless mirror-universe Archer overthrows Captain Forrest to capture the USS Defiant, a Federation ship from another universe's future, adrift in Tholian space.
ent-4x19: With the ISS Enterprise destroyed, Archer seizes the Defiant and plots to become emperor, crushing T'Pol's revolt, until Hoshi poisons him and takes the throne.
ent-4x20: As Earth hosts coalition talks, Trip and T'Pol learn a baby has been engineered from their DNA, a trail leading to John Paxton's xenophobic Terra Prime movement.
ent-4x21: Paxton seizes a Martian array and threatens Starfleet Command if non-humans stay in the solar system, while the cloned daughter of Trip and T'Pol sickens and dies.
ent-4x22: Facing a hard choice, Riker relives on the Enterprise-D holodeck the final mission of Archer's Enterprise, on the eve of the Federation's founding, in which Trip dies.
flm-01: Admiral Kirk reclaims the newly refitted Enterprise to intercept a vast cloud bound for Earth, at whose core lies V'Ger, an old NASA Voyager probe seeking its creator.
flm-02: Marooned for fifteen years, Khan seizes the starship Reliant and the Genesis device to take revenge on Kirk, and victory in the Mutara Nebula costs Spock his life.
flm-03: Learning McCoy carries Spock's spirit, Kirk steals the Enterprise for Genesis, losing his son and his ship to the Klingon Kruge before Spock is restored on Vulcan.
flm-04: An alien probe ravages Earth while calling to extinct humpback whales, so Kirk's crew takes a captured Klingon ship back to 1986 San Francisco to bring two home.
flm-05: Spock's half-brother Sybok takes hostages on Nimbus III to lure the Enterprise-A, then commandeers it to cross the Great Barrier in search of God at the galaxy's center.
flm-06: After the moon Praxis explodes, the Klingons seek peace, but Chancellor Gorkon's assassination lands Kirk and McCoy on Rura Penthe while conspirators on both sides scheme against peace.
flm-07: El-Aurian Soran will destroy stars to reenter the Nexus, and Picard, having lost the Enterprise-D, recruits Kirk, trapped there since 2293, who dies stopping him.
flm-08: Joining a Borg battle against orders, Picard pursues a Borg sphere back to 2063, where he must protect Zefram Cochrane's first warp flight and confront the Borg Queen.
flm-09: Picard rebels against Starfleet when he learns it has conspired with the Son'a to forcibly relocate the Ba'ku from their youth-restoring planet, whose rings they plan to harvest.
flm-10: Shinzon, Picard's clone raised in the mines of Remus, seizes Romulus and lures the Enterprise into a trap, and Data sacrifices himself to stop his thalaron weapon.
flm-11: Nero, a Romulan from the future, rewrites history by killing Kirk's father and destroying Vulcan, and a young Kirk and Spock, guided by Spock's older self, stop him.
flm-12: Hunting the terrorist John Harrison to Qo'noS, Kirk learns he is Khan, revived by Admiral Marcus to arm Starfleet for war, then dies, briefly, saving the Enterprise.
flm-13: Lured into a nebula, the Enterprise is shredded by Krall's swarm, and its stranded crew, aided by the scavenger Jaylah, must keep him from attacking Starbase Yorktown.
flm-14: Recruited by Section 31, Starfleet's secret division, former Terran emperor Philippa Georgiou falls in with a team of misfits to recover a doomsday weapon from her bloody past.
ld-1x01: Ensign Tendi's first day aboard the USS Cerritos brings new friends Mariner, Boimler, and Rutherford, a secret order for Boimler to spy on Mariner, and an infectious outbreak.
ld-1x02: Chasing a wayward Klingon general who gave them the slip, Boimler feels outshone by the effortless Mariner, while Rutherford quits engineering to try other jobs aboard the Cerritos.
ld-1x03: Freeman's crackdown on buffer time leaves the overworked crew collapsing, while Mariner and Commander Ransom's feud boils over when their away team is taken captive.
ld-1x04: Freeman assigns Mariner every miserable job aboard to make her quit, until both are trapped by runaway terraforming goo, while Tendi disrupts Lieutenant O'Connor's bid for ascension.
ld-1x05: Boimler's too-good-to-be-true new girlfriend, Barbara, arouses Mariner's suspicion, while Tendi and Rutherford covet the flashier gear of a bigger starship.
ld-1x06: Well-meaning Ensign Fletcher's shortcuts drag Mariner and Boimler into trouble, while Rutherford's holodeck training assistant, Badgey, turns murderous during Tendi's lesson.
ld-1x07: Mariner strains to impress an Academy friend who now captains her own ship, while a transporter glitch leaves Boimler out of phase and quarantined among medical curiosities.
ld-1x08: Tendi, Rutherford, Mariner, and Boimler are hauled before an alien court and made to testify about scattered incidents they glimpsed, which turn out to be connected.
ld-1x09: Taking over Boimler's command-training holoprogram, Mariner turns it into a movie-style epic starring herself as the villain Vindicta, working through her resentment of her mother, Captain Freeman.
ld-1x10: The Pakleds, armed with stolen tech, cripple the Cerritos and kill Lieutenant Shaxs, Mariner's secret as Freeman's daughter comes out, and Riker's Titan arrives, taking Boimler with it.
ld-2x01: Commander Ransom absorbs a strange alien energy that turns him into a towering, godlike menace, while Mariner and Freeman awkwardly try working together as mother and daughter.
ld-2x02: The ensigns struggle to warm to Jet Manhaver, Boimler's replacement, on a mission to a collector's hoard, while Boimler finds Riker's Titan more intense than he bargained for.
ld-2x03: Mariner and Tendi retrieve a keepsake for Dr. T'Ana, Boimler schemes to meet the visiting Tom Paris, and Rutherford is unnerved when the late Shaxs turns up alive.
ld-2x04: Checking reports of a mugato, the venomous horned ape, on a remote planet, the Cerritos away team runs into poachers who hunt the creatures.
ld-2x05: Rumors of a legendary, exclusive Starfleet bash send Mariner and Boimler searching, while the bridge crew escorts a Doopler envoy whose species copies itself whenever it feels embarrassed.
ld-2x06: Anomaly consolidation day stirs mixed feelings among the ensigns, while Captain Freeman seeks a peace deal with the Pakleds on their homeworld and a Pakled spy slips aboard.
ld-2x07: Mariner and Boimler crash on a barren planet with AGIMUS, a megalomaniacal computer they were transporting, while Billups has to outshine an old rival as an engineer.
ld-2x08: A visiting consultant puts the Cerritos through drills that swap the ensigns' duties with the bridge crew's, and Boimler throws himself too fully into a Borg assimilation scenario.
ld-2x09: On a long warp haul, Boimler seeks a friend on the bridge, while junior officers aboard a Klingon ship and a Vulcan ship live out parallel days.
ld-2x10: The Cerritos supports another starship's first contact mission, which goes awry, and the crew's triumph ends with Captain Freeman arrested for the destruction of the Pakled homeworld.
ld-3x01: While Captain Freeman stands trial, accused of destroying the Pakled homeworld, her daughter Mariner leads her friends on an unauthorized mission to clear the captain's name.
ld-3x02: Mariner questions how Commander Ransom chooses his away teams during a mission to a tropical paradise, while Boimler decides to take a daring leap in his career.
ld-3x03: Stone orbs at a remote science outpost start making people's fantasies real, just as Tendi begins her first day training to become a senior science officer.
ld-3x04: Old grudges flare between Delta Shift and the trio of Mariner, Boimler, and Tendi, while the Cerritos engineers are ordered onto mandatory relaxation leave.
ld-3x05: Mariner and Boimler try to sign up new Starfleet recruits at an interstellar career fair, while Rutherford sets out to test his own limits.
ld-3x06: The Cerritos makes an unplanned stop at Deep Space 9, where Freeman meets Colonel Kira and the ensigns explore the station's storied Promenade.
ld-3x07: Peanut Hamper, the exocomp who abandoned the Cerritos in battle, tries to redeem herself among kindly aliens on a remote world, but old habits prove hard to shake.
ld-3x08: Boimler shoots Crisis Point 2: Paradoxus, a holodeck sequel he fears can never match the original, with his friends pulled into the production.
ld-3x09: A reporter embeds aboard the Cerritos, and Captain Freeman, anxious about how her crew will be portrayed, struggles to keep things under control.
ld-3x10: To save the California-class ships from retirement, the Cerritos races an automated Texas-class starship on a mission contest, only for the drone ship to turn hostile.
ld-4x01: The ensigns help ferry the retired USS Voyager to a museum, where a transporter mishap fuses two Cerritos officers into one, echoing an infamous incident from its past.
ld-4x02: Now lieutenants, Mariner schemes to get herself demoted while Rutherford chases a promotion and Boimler moves into new quarters, as a cute, bone-sucking Moopsy runs loose aboard.
ld-4x03: Boimler takes charge of his first away mission, exploring a vast alien megastructure, and quickly discovers how much responsibility the job carries.
ld-4x04: Summoned home to Orion for a family wedding, Tendi brings Mariner along and must face her family and the past she left to join Starfleet.
ld-4x05: A party-loving Betazoid delegation visits the Cerritos, and its uninhibited mood spreads through the crew with unruly results.
ld-4x06: The Cerritos visits Ferenginar as Grand Nagus Rom weighs bringing the Ferengi into the Federation, and Captain Freeman works to seal the deal amid Ferengi-style hospitality.
ld-4x07: Three rogue machines resurface to plague the Cerritos crew: Rutherford's hologram Badgey, the scheming computer AGIMUS, and the treacherous exocomp Peanut Hamper.
ld-4x08: Trapped in a cave during a routine mission, the friends pass the time trading tales of their earlier cave misadventures.
ld-4x09: Worried about Mariner's reckless streak, Captain Freeman gives the ensigns an ultra-safe assignment, but Mariner's self-destructive behavior pulls her toward real danger.
ld-4x10: Mariner confronts her past when the raider destroying ships proves to be led by Nick Locarno, the disgraced former Starfleet cadet she once knew.
ld-5x01: A quantum fissure brings the Cerritos face to face with a duplicate ship from another reality, crewed by alternate versions of its own officers.
ld-5x02: Tendi scrambles to defuse a conflict, while Mariner and Boimler set out to thwart a scheme by profit-hungry capitalists.
ld-5x03: On a visit to a luxury resort in space, the friends end up hunting runaway nanites loose on the premises.
ld-5x04: Dr. Migleemo turns up the heat in the kitchen, while Mariner nurses a grudge and plots a revenge best served cold.
ld-5x05: A visit to the notoriously run-down Starbase 80 finds Ransom overdoing the disinfectant gel and Mariner growing paranoid that she has been cursed.
ld-5x06: A troubled ensign partners with Mariner, while the Cerritos plays host to negotiations between two rival civilizations.
ld-5x07: A covert survey of a pre-warp society turns into a girls' trip for the Cerritos women sent undercover among the locals.
ld-5x08: While the friends throw a pumpkin-carving party below, the Cerritos's senior officers get a turn in the spotlight on the upper decks.
ld-5x09: William Boimler, the transporter double now captaining the USS Anaximander, commands alternate versions of Garak, Bashir, T'Pol, and Dax to seal the quantum fissures tearing at the multiverse.
ld-5x10: The quantum fissure crisis comes to a head as the Cerritos crew makes its final stand to keep the multiverse from collapsing, closing out their adventures.
pic-1x01: Retired to his vineyard, Picard is sought out by Dahj, a woman hunted by assassins, and after her death learns she was Data's synthetic daughter, with a twin.
pic-1x02: Rebuffed by Starfleet, Picard investigates Dahj's origins with synthetic researcher Agnes Jurati and turns to estranged former aide Raffi Musiker, as a secret Romulan cabal tracks his search.
pic-1x03: Unaware she is synthetic, Soji works on a Romulan-held Borg cube under Hugh, while Picard, rebuffed by Raffi, hires pilot Cristóbal Rios to find Bruce Maddox.
pic-1x04: Picard detours to Vashti, where he resettled Romulan refugees, and enlists Elnor, the Qowat Milat-raised youth he left behind, before Seven of Nine arrives to rescue La Sirena.
pic-1x05: On Freecloud, Picard's crew cons crime boss Bjayzl to free Bruce Maddox, Seven of Nine avenges Icheb, and Jurati secretly kills Maddox.
pic-1x06: Facing his Borg trauma, Picard boards the Romulan-held cube to reach Soji, as Narek uses a Romulan puzzle box to pry her homeworld's location from her memories.
pic-1x07: At Nepenthe, the home of Riker and Troi, Picard helps Soji come to terms with herself, while on the cube Narissa kills Hugh and Elnor makes a stand.
pic-1x08: Picard's crew learns the Zhat Vash, a secret Romulan sect, orchestrated the Mars attack to stop synthetic life, while Seven links with the cube's Borg to fight Narissa.
pic-1x09: Reaching Coppelius, the synthetics' hidden homeworld, Picard's crew meets Altan Soong and the android Sutra, who plans to summon machine allies as a Romulan armada closes in.
pic-1x10: Picard persuades Soji to halt the synthetics' beacon as Riker's fleet faces down the Romulans, then dies, wakes in a synthetic body, and grants Data his final wish.
pic-2x01: A Borg ship emerging from a space anomaly asks to join the Federation, and Picard's reunion with his crew ends with the Stargazer's self-destruct and Q's return.
pic-2x02: Q strands Picard in a dystopian 2401 ruled by the Confederation of Earth, where he rounds up his displaced crew and seizes a captive Borg Queen to escape.
pic-2x03: Elnor dies as the crew escapes to 2024 Los Angeles to find a mysterious Watcher, while Picard and Jurati extract what they can from the Borg Queen.
pic-2x04: Picard turns to a younger Guinan and meets Tallinn, the Watcher, while Rios is detained by immigration agents and Jurati strikes a bargain with the Borg Queen.
pic-2x05: Renée Picard, an astronaut bound for Europa and Picard's ancestor, proves key to the altered timeline, as Q manipulates Adam Soong and Seven and Raffi spring Rios.
pic-2x06: The crew sneaks into a pre-launch gala to shield astronaut Renée Picard from harm, with a Borg-influenced Jurati stealing the show, while Kore Soong uncovers her father's experiments.
pic-2x07: Tallinn enters a comatose Picard's mind to help him face memories of his mother, while Seven and Raffi hunt Jurati and Rios hides his origins from Teresa.
pic-2x08: Picard and Guinan must talk their way out of FBI custody before the Europa launch, while Seven and Raffi confront a Jurati now merging with the Borg Queen.
pic-2x09: A Borg collective led by the Jurati-Queen hybrid besieges Château Picard, where Picard faces his mother's death, and Jurati ultimately leaves Earth to remake the Borg.
pic-2x10: Racing the Europa launch clock, Picard saves Renée from Adam Soong, learns why a dying Q brought him here, and returns to 2401, leaving Rios behind in 2024.
pic-3x01: Answering Beverly Crusher's coded plea, Picard and Riker talk their way onto the USS Titan and find her hiding with a grown son, Jack, as Vadic closes in.
pic-3x02: Aboard the Titan, Picard learns Jack is his son as Vadic demands the young man's surrender, while Raffi, tracking a stolen weapon, finds her mysterious handler is Worf.
pic-3x03: Picard reels at being a father as the Titan plays cat and mouse with Vadic inside a nebula, and Raffi and Worf trace the plot to renegade Changelings.
pic-3x04: Trapped and powerless inside the nebula, the Titan drifts toward destruction as Picard, Riker, and Shaw confront old wounds, until the nebula's hidden nature offers an escape.
pic-3x05: Intercepted by Starfleet, Picard must learn whether Ro Laren, his old officer turned Intelligence agent, is friend or Changeling, and she gives her life to expose Starfleet's infiltration.
pic-3x06: Now fugitives, the Titan crew enlists Geordi La Forge to break into Daystrom Station, where they learn Picard's original body was stolen and find a revived Data.
pic-3x07: To learn Vadic's motives, Picard lures her into a trap aboard the Titan, uncovering Starfleet's wartime experiments on Changelings, but the gambit backfires and she seizes the ship.
pic-3x08: Vadic, holding the Titan's bridge, demands Jack for the crew's lives, while Data battles Lore for their shared body and, winning, helps the crew retake the ship.
pic-3x09: Jack's visions lead to the Borg Queen, whose Changeling-aided plot turns Starfleet's young crews into drones on Frontier Day, and Picard's old crew takes the restored Enterprise-D.
pic-3x10: Picard's old crew takes the Enterprise-D against the Borg Queen's cube hidden in Jupiter to free Jack and the fleet, and Seven inherits a new Enterprise.
pro-1x01-02: Young prisoners on the mining colony Tars Lamora, led by Dal, commandeer the derelict starship Protostar and escape the Diviner, taking his daughter Gwyn along against her will.
pro-1x03: With Dal as self-appointed captain, the untrained crew takes its first lessons from Hologram Janeway, then must steer the Protostar off a deadly cosmic collision course.
pro-1x04: On their first away mission, the crew explores a planet that conjures each member's deepest desires, only to find the living world is luring them in to feed.
pro-1x05: Stranded on a hostile planet, the crew must rely on their captive Gwyn to survive, while the Diviner's relentless robot enforcer Drednok closes in.
pro-1x06: Dal runs the Kobayashi Maru on the newfound holodeck with a crew of simulated Starfleet legends to prove himself, while Gwyn searches for her place aboard.
pro-1x07: Dal's old mentor, Nandi, talks him into using the crew's Starfleet guise to swindle a newly contacted species, and the scheme shows why Starfleet's protocols exist.
pro-1x08: An anomaly splinters the Protostar into pockets of different time, and Hologram Janeway must bring each isolated crew member back in sync before the ship destroys itself.
pro-1x09: Giving up their dream of reaching Starfleet, the crew turns back to Tars Lamora to free the prisoners they left behind, a seemingly unwinnable mission.
pro-1x10: When their liberation plan unravels, the crew improvises to free Tars Lamora's prisoners, and Gwyn learns her father's grim purpose for the Protostar.
pro-1x11: Seeking asylum at a remote Federation relay station, the crew discovers the Protostar carries a hidden weapon that turns nearby Starfleet systems against themselves.
pro-1x12: Exploring a dormant Borg cube, the crew stirs its drones back to life, and Zero makes a desperate gamble to keep everyone from assimilation.
pro-1x13: A distress call leads the crew to a colony whose whole culture imitates a long-ago Starfleet visit, and saving it means playing the roles it expects.
pro-1x14: Trying to book passage into Federation space, the crew unknowingly crosses paths with the real Vice Admiral Janeway, who is hunting the Protostar.
pro-1x15: Caught in the Romulan Neutral Zone, Dal and his friends meet a rogue geneticist who reveals that Dal was engineered from the DNA of many species.
pro-1x16: As a Starfleet admiral probes the Protostar crew's pasts, the Diviner recalls how his homeworld, Solum, was ruined, and the vengeful mission it inspired.
pro-1x17: A mysterious malfunction traps the crew in the holodeck, where they can no longer tell what is programmed from what is real.
pro-1x18: To warn Starfleet about the weapon aboard their ship, the crew tries a risky experiment that swaps Dal's mind with that of Vice Admiral Janeway.
pro-1x19: With a Federation armada gathered around the Protostar, the crew races to stop the weapon inside it from turning Starfleet's ships against one another.
pro-1x20: The crew sacrifices the Protostar to shield the fleet from its weapon, and as the Diviner's scheme collapses, the young outlaws earn a future in Starfleet.
pro-2x01: Now Starfleet trainees, Dal and his friends join Admiral Janeway aboard the USS Voyager-A to study the rift left by the Protostar, though Dal is restless for action.
pro-2x02: Gwyn meets an old adversary on her ancestral world, Solum, as Janeway confides to the cadets what their mission to the rift truly puts at risk.
pro-2x03: Dal's team slips through the time rift to comb Solum for the missing Chakotay, while Gwyn, backed by her father, defies the militant Asencia.
pro-2x04: Decades apart in time, Voyager's crew and the cadets aboard the Infinity join forces to keep Gwyn alive, and an unknown messenger makes contact with her.
pro-2x05: Back aboard Voyager and closely watched, the cadets work to decode a secret message that their unknown benefactor entrusted to Murf.
pro-2x06: Planning to steal the Infinity before it is scrapped, Dal and the crew program holographic doubles of themselves to cover their absence aboard Voyager.
pro-2x07: A shortcut through a Borg transwarp conduit leaves Dal and his friends under the thumb of a demanding Kazon.
pro-2x08: A detour to a colony of noncorporeal beings brings Zero an offer of a physical body, while Janeway uncovers what Dal is really planning.
pro-2x09: Reaching the coordinates at last, the Infinity crew finds a hidden planet and learns who their mysterious messenger has been all along.
pro-2x10: Fleeing pursuers that erase whatever they touch from time, the Infinity's crew and a new ally hunt for an escape route while Voyager mounts a rescue.
pro-2x11: Wesley Crusher's timely help leads the cadets to the lost Protostar, but its marooned guardian, Chakotay, is wary of their offer of rescue.
pro-2x12: Chakotay and the cadets hatch a risky plan to get the grounded Protostar airborne again, one that requires the starship to sail before it can fly.
pro-2x13: Collecting bosonite on a desolate planet, the crew is overrun by vicious, genetically engineered tribbles bred there by a Klingon researcher.
pro-2x14: When the Protostar links up with Voyager again, the crew starts skipping from one alternate reality to the next, the mirror universe among them.
pro-2x15: With their mission nearly done, the two crews of Voyager and the Protostar face Asencia, their enemy from Solum, who returns with startling new abilities.
pro-2x16: Outgunned by Asencia's uncannily advanced weapons, the allied crews resort to a string of gambles that leave the cadets in serious danger.
pro-2x17: As the Federation and Solum edge toward war, Gwyn talks the cadets into an undercover operation to collect intelligence and free her father, Ilthuran.
pro-2x18: Janeway schemes to break her crew out of Asencia's prison, where they are locked up alongside a furious being taken from the Loom.
pro-2x19: Cornered, Asencia unleashes a total offensive against the Federation that could wipe out subspace, as Wesley leads the cadets in a bid to set the timeline right.
pro-2x20: The cadets take on Asencia in a decisive fight over Solum's fate and the timeline, until a devastating alien incursion throws their final plan into chaos.
sa-1x01: Caleb, a fugitive hacker, is offered a place in Starfleet Academy's first class in a century by Chancellor Nahla Ake, the captain who sent his mother to prison.
sa-1x02: Uneasy about his future, Caleb must escort the daughter of a visiting leader from a onetime Federation ally, and starts to grasp what the Academy is really for.
sa-1x03: As the cadets vie for a spot on an elite Academy team, an escalating prank war with a rival school strains their new friendships and a budding romance.
sa-1x04: When a crisis threatens a beloved yet notorious species with extinction, one cadet must face his past and his strained family ties, while Nahla races to save them.
sa-1x05: SAM, a holographic cadet, tackles a centuries-old Starfleet puzzle and learns to chart her own course, while Nahla assists another chancellor with a complicated alien rite.
sa-1x06: On their first training exercise, aboard a derelict ship, the cadets meet a lethal new foe, and Nahla gambles everything on help from a source she cannot trust.
sa-1x07: On break, the cadets weigh family expectations against their dreams, as a would-be captain plots to rewrite her past and a noble cadet is called home to serve.
sa-1x08: A visiting instructor takes an unconventional approach to helping the cadets work through recent trauma, while one cadet confronts a challenge that reshapes her future.
sa-1x09: At year's end, Caleb is torn between his old goals and the home he has found at the Academy, while Nahla bends the rules to keep her word.
sa-1x10: An old enemy returns to menace the Federation, and Nahla must outthink a foe bent on personal revenge while the cadets and instructors attempt a near-impossible rescue.
snw-1x01: Pike leaves his Montana retreat to rescue Number One from Kiley 279, a world racing toward warp and civil war, while wrestling with his vision of his fate.
snw-1x02: An ancient relic on a comet blocks the Enterprise's effort to divert it from an inhabited world, and Uhura must decipher its music while zealots called Shepherds interfere.
snw-1x03: An illness that drives victims toward light sweeps the Enterprise, and only Number One stays well, forcing her to confront her hidden identity as a genetically modified Illyrian.
snw-1x04: The Gorn ambush a supply run, and security chief La'an Noonien-Singh, who survived their predation as a child, helps Pike outwit them inside a brown dwarf's atmosphere.
snw-1x05: A visit from his fiancée T'Pring leaves Spock trapped in her body, and vice versa, just as he and Pike must negotiate with the prickly Rhylkans.
snw-1x06: Protecting a revered child on the idyllic world Majalis, Pike reunites with his old love Alora, then learns its paradise depends on the boy's suffering inside a machine.
snw-1x07: Lured into a trap on a relief mission, the Enterprise is seized by the pirate Captain Angel, who demands the release of Sybok, Spock's estranged brother.
snw-1x08: A consciousness in a nebula recasts the crew as figures in the fairy tale Dr. M'Benga reads to his dying daughter, Rukiya, and offers her a new life.
snw-1x09: At the wreck of the USS Peregrine on an icy world, the landing party is hunted by Gorn hatchlings, and an infected Hemmer sacrifices himself to save them.
snw-1x10: Pike's future self shows him how escaping his fate plays out, a Romulan confrontation that ends in war, and Pike accepts his destiny as Una is arrested.
snw-2x01: Answering La'an's distress call, Spock defies orders and takes the Enterprise into disputed space, where the crew uncovers a plot to reignite war with the Klingons.
snw-2x02: Facing court-martial for hiding her Illyrian heritage, Una is defended by Neera Ketoul, an estranged childhood friend, who frames her case as a plea for asylum and wins.
